Student-generated instructional materials such as course summaries and problem sets are amongst the instructional strategies that reflect active learning and constructivist philosophy.\n\nThe contributions of this work are twofold: 1) We introduce a practical implementation of inside-outside learning strategy in an undergraduate deep learning course and will share our experiences in incorporating student-generated instructional materials learning strategy in course design, and 2) We develop a context-aware deep learning framework to draw insights from the student-generated materials for (i) Detecting anomalies in group activities and (ii) Predicting the median quiz performance of students in each group.
